concerns.text: Tasks T011 and T012 cite non-existent or unverified HuggingFace dataset IDs (`HuggingFaceH4/imo`, `HuggingFaceH4/ipho`) and a generic `nvidia/OpenScience` source. FR-001 mandates downloading IMO/IPhO and the curated 'OpenSci-Reason' dataset. The tasks fail to specify the exact, verified source for the 'OpenSci-Reason' curation logic (removing factual Q&A) required by the spec, risking a failure to load the required data and violating the 'Verified Accuracy' constitution principle.

FR-003 explicitly mandates generating up to 3 distinct candidate responses per prompt for the OpenSci-Reason dataset. Task T014 only describes implementing a generic 'inference runner' without a specific sub-task to loop generation or enforce the '3 candidates' requirement. This is a semantic weakening of the functional requirement, as the deliverable (a runner) does not guarantee the specific output volume mandated by the spec.

FR-009 requires a power analysis to justify the N=500 sample size. Task T033 incorrectly restricts the input to a 'fixed N=500' and asks for a report based on that fixed number, rather than implementing the logic to calculate the required sample size or verify the power of the actual dataset (which may vary if curation T012 reduces the count below 500). This silently relaxes the requirement to perform a dynamic validation of the sample size sufficiency.

SC-005 requires measuring robustness by testing the sensitivity of the correlation coefficient to the exclusion of low-confidence prompts. Task T035 only implements sensitivity analysis for the LME interaction p-value, failing to explicitly address the correlation coefficient sensitivity required by the success criterion. This is a dropped acceptance criterion.

The spec's edge case for RAM failure (7GB limit) mandates a fallback to a 'smaller quantized model OR a distilled model' with a mechanism to verify the fallback fits. Task T020 defines the fallback logic as a '4-bit quantized 2B OR distilled 3B' without a mechanism to dynamically detect the specific RAM overhead or verify the fallback model actually fits. This risks a silent OOM crash if the fallback also exceeds the limit, violating the 'Inference Constraints' constitution principle.
